back: Independent southern African states (Tanzania, Zambia, Botswana, Mozambique, Angola; Zimbabwe from 1980) that co-ordinated support for liberation from the mid-1970s.

front: Which country hosted ZANLA's rear bases after 1975?
When did Mozambique close its border with Rhodesia?
Name three camps raided by Rhodesian forces.
back: Nyadzonia (August 1976) and Chimoio (November 1977) in Mozambique; Freedom Camp (October 1978) in Zambia.

front: Where was the OAU Liberation Committee based?
back: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (set up in 1963).

front: How did the Frontline States help the liberation struggle?
back: Bases and training, transit for recruits and refugees, diplomacy (Patriotic Front, Lusaka 1979), pressure in negotiations, sanctions and border closures.

front: Which outside powers backed which army?
back: The Soviet Union mainly backed ZIPRA; China mainly backed ZANLA.
